\subsection{Outlook: forthcoming instantiations}\label{sec:outlook}
This paper isolates a math-only emergence calculus.
It uses a \emph{theory package} (lens/definability, completion, audit).
It is paired with the six primitive moves that change what theories can exist and what objects they recognize.
A series of companion papers will instantiate this calculus in multiple domains (with domain-specific choices of lenses, bridges, and audits) while keeping the present framework fixed:
\begin{itemize}
  \item mathematics theories,
  \item physics theories as families of effective closures across scales,
  \item life and cognition as theory stacks,
  \item conscious entities as theories,
  \item societies and civilizations,
  \item the universe as a “theorist”.
\end{itemize}
We intentionally do not include details here; the purpose of this paragraph is only to indicate scope and to delineate the boundary between the general calculus proved in this paper and its forthcoming instantiations.

conclusion: An adjacent meta-theoretic question, deferred to future work, is whether the accepted internal instrument family can itself certify both its soundness and its completeness for exact-six judgments formulable inside the same regime. Future work
expanded_source_wording_tex:
An adjacent meta-theoretic question, deferred to future work, is
whether the accepted internal instrument family can itself certify
both its soundness and its completeness for exact-six judgments
formulable inside the same regime. A plausible sharp formulation is
that no internal argument should be expected to accomplish all three
of the following at once:
\begin{enumerate}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item establish the scoped exact-six claim;
  \item certify the soundness of the accepted instrument family;
  \item certify the completeness of that family for exact-six
    judgments expressible inside the same regime.
\end{enumerate}
Such self-certification limits are of a piece with the classical
G{\"o}del--L{\"o}b tradition on internal consistency and provability
statements~\citep{Godel1931,Lob1955}. This question is not part of
the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:scoped-exact-six} and does not weaken
or retract the theorem's scoped conclusion. It is taken up as a
follow-on direction in Section~\ref{sec:future-work}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
A formalization of the meta-limit described in
Section~\ref{subsec:meta-limit} would target a three-way
impossibility statement: no internal argument can simultaneously
establish the scoped exact-six claim, certify the soundness of the
accepted instrument family, and certify its completeness for
exact-six judgments formulable inside the same regime.
Theorem~\ref{thm:scoped-exact-six} would remain intact under such a
result; the additional content would be a precise account of
self-certification boundaries. A closely related open question is
\emph{recognition-completeness}: whether every finite audited feature of a
description in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}} reduces to the six role meanings --- the recognition
hypothesis on which Theorem~\ref{thm:upper-bound-classification} is conditional
(Remark~\ref{rem:recognition-open}). Candidate witnesses against it --- finite
conservation laws and emergent composite obstructions --- would, if irreducible,
populate the genuine-seventh-role category; establishing or refuting their
reducibility is left to future work.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Section 2} records preliminaries and scope: finite host mathematics, primitive labels and levels, claim strengths, status discipline, and the global nonclaim conventions.
\item
  \emph{Sections 3 and 4} define the finite audited calculus: the finite typed domain, the central object \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) as a finite typed tuple, theory packages, instruments, source-of-truth records, audit records, visibility bridges, directed-cell records, pair-observable records, promotion bridges, and the per-cell profile schema.
\item
  \emph{Section 5} records the status and defect semantics: the seven status families, the per-component defect schemas, the visibility-defect family, and the classifier priority orders.
\item
  \emph{Sections 6--8} prove the finite theorem spine: the no-total-algebra theorem and the four core finite-interaction theorems (Section 6); the nine descent/packaging/completion/strictness theorems (Section 7); and the four cohomological no-drive theorems on graph-supported drive (Section 8).
\item
  \emph{Section 9} records the countermodel atlas in main-text form, with full sheets for CM\_1--CM\_6 and named pointers to CM\_7--CM\_12. The full twelve-countermodel atlas is recorded in Appendix C.
\item
  \emph{Section 10} records promotion and stacking: the promotion-bridge schema, the eight-gate machinery, the promotion-status consequences of the classifier, Theorems 19--21, the Toy22 strict-bridge example, and the stacking claims not proved.
\item
  \emph{Section 11} records instruments, visibility, and rotating audit: the instrument-indexed claim semantics, the classifier priority, the visibility/suppression discipline, the no-overreading theorem (Theorem 23), the same-level self-audit failure theorem (Theorem 24), the \(P_{6}\leftarrow P_{6}\) status separation, the rotating-audit chain and bridge, the finite rotating-audit theorem (Theorem 25), and the instrument-transfer rule.
\item
  \emph{Section 12} records the abstract-interpretation model family: the host data, the realized fragment \(P_{1}/P_{2}/P_{4}/P_{5}/P_{6}\), Theorems 26--28 (closure as packaging, descent as sound transformer, representability as fixedness), and Model Theorem 29.
\item
  \emph{Section 13} records the four scoped model realizations (PICA, Cantor strict-bridge, abstract interpretation, graph/cohomology), Model Theorems 33 and 34, the combined model-realization matrix, and the cross-model role-coverage observation.
\item
  \emph{Section 14} records the secondary high-structure semantics: the finite decorated double-category fragment and the recovery theorems 30--32 (descent-square recovery, completion-pasting recovery, strict extension as no-filler).
\item
  \emph{Section 15} records the Lean 4 validation artifact, the manifest-driven validator, and Proposition 35.
\item
  \emph{Section 16} records limitations, nonclaims, and future work, with the final paper-inclusion nonclaim block of thirty-six entries.
\item
  \emph{Section 17} records the conclusion.
\item
  \emph{Appendices A--H} record the long-form supplementary material: full definitions and tables (A), long proofs (B), the full countermodel atlas (C), the four model-realization sheets (D), the high-structure semantics extension (E), the Lean mechanization appendix (F), the dependency graph (G), and the deferred and dropped claims register (H).
\end{itemize}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{enumerate}
\def\arabic{enumi}.{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  PICA is not the universal six-bird algebra: \(\mathsf{PICAReal}_{\mathrm{fin}}\) realizes a declared finite stochastic fragment, not the whole calculus.
\item
  The recovered \(6\times 6\) multiplicity count is a PICA-profile model fact under the cell profile \(\lambda_{\mathrm{PICA}}\), not a universal \(6\times 6\) law.
\item
  Raw PICA status is not formal status without recovery and classifier check; the formal classifier verdict is the authoritative cell status.
\item
  Directed-cell status \(\texttt{action}\) does not imply pair-realness; pair-realness requires the source/visibility/audit/threshold conjunction of Subsubsection 13.2.7.
\item
  A fallback record does not by itself support a real pair source-of-truth; it supports at most \(\texttt{real\_provisional}\).
\item
  Ablation evidence in \(\mathsf{Abl}\) is model-realization evidence, not theorem-grade evidence, in the absence of an admissible bridge to a theorem-grade claim.
\item
  A \(P_3\) route mismatch is not a \(\mathrm{P6}_{\mathrm{drive}}\) assertion in the sense of Section 8: the two are connected only through an admissible drive bridge.
\item
  A dirty record cannot support a real claim under any host configuration of \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{PICA}}\).
\item
  PICA realizes a finite stochastic fragment, and not the entirety of \(\mathbf{BirdInt}^{\mathrm{aud}}_{\mathrm{fin}}\); this restates the fragment discipline of Subsection 13.1.2.
\item
  Implementation correctness of any concrete PICA implementation is future work and is not certified by this realization theorem; the Lean validation record of Section 15 is a separate, manifest-scoped artifact.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:e11}]
Fix a complete matched comparison.  If a linked structural effect exists,
the accepted channel supplies difference-making for that exact pair, and
the concrete comparator supplies either a support witness $(z,z')$ or
closure inequality.  Empty $\Delta_{\rm stack}$ excludes reproduction of
the outcome on unrevised support.  If a carried E11-local
\texttt{CompiledRewriteRecord} and the certified
\texttt{E4CompiledInstitutionalRewrite.holds} host bridge are also present,
the constitutive case holds.  This is an E4-shaped interface, not an import of
the actual E4 theorem or record type; the general E4-to-E11 bridge remains
open.  If no such evidence exists, the comparison-wide negation in
\texttt{StackActiveEvidence} gives the stack-active case.

conclusion: The catalog is intentionally incomplete. The following candidates have recognizable shapes but do not yet possess a distinct theorem, obstruction set, and recognition interface. Global or conscious access. Simultaneous descent into memory, action, and report may combine E6, E7, E12, and E13 without adding a new law. Phenomenality is outside the present apparatus. Play or sandboxed obstruction sampling. This currently appears to be E9 under a gated risk budget unless transfer from sandbox to live repair supplies a new obstruction. Boundary discovery dynamics. E12 classifies a candidate boundary; it does not state how a carrier searches the boundary lattice. Transported gates and norms. E13 transports repair. A separate P2-transport theorem may be needed for norms, standards, and regulatory gates. Distributed exposure and price discovery. A multi-carrier E6/E9 system may model markets or collective sensing, but standard aggregation results must not be merely renamed. Reproduction, heredity, and evolutionary closure. The E-series treats repair and adaptation of a declared carrier. Replication, heritable variation, population selection, ecological inheritance, and open-ended lineage innovation require additional carrier and source machinery. The life-focused substrate paper likewise separates bounded competencies from autonomous open-ended evolution . Abiogenesis and origin-of-life transitions. No theorem here selects the first E-system from nonliving chemistry or proves that the D1–D6 package is necessary and sufficient for life.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The catalog is intentionally incomplete.  The following candidates have
recognizable shapes but do not yet possess a distinct theorem, obstruction
set, and recognition interface.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Global or conscious access.} Simultaneous descent into
  memory, action, and report may combine E6, E7, E12, and E13 without adding
  a new law.  Phenomenality is outside the present apparatus.
  \item \textbf{Play or sandboxed obstruction sampling.} This currently
  appears to be E9 under a gated risk budget unless transfer from sandbox to
  live repair supplies a new obstruction.
  \item \textbf{Boundary discovery dynamics.} E12 classifies a candidate
  boundary; it does not state how a carrier searches the boundary lattice.
  \item \textbf{Transported gates and norms.} E13 transports repair.  A
  separate P2-transport theorem may be needed for norms, standards, and
  regulatory gates.
  \item \textbf{Distributed exposure and price discovery.} A multi-carrier
  E6/E9 system may model markets or collective sensing, but standard
  aggregation results must not be merely renamed.
  \item \textbf{Reproduction, heredity, and evolutionary closure.} The
  E-series treats repair and adaptation of a declared carrier.  Replication,
  heritable variation, population selection, ecological inheritance, and
  open-ended lineage innovation require additional carrier and source
  machinery.  The life-focused substrate paper likewise separates bounded
  competencies from autonomous open-ended evolution
  \citep{Tsiokos2026Life}.
  \item \textbf{Abiogenesis and origin-of-life transitions.} No theorem here
  selects the first E-system from nonliving chemistry or proves that the
  D1--D6 package is necessary and sufficient for life.
\end{itemize}

The Six Birds corpus through Foundations~IV certifies \emph{states}: each of its laws fixes a single map,
quotient, package, or declared finite family and proves a static classification about it. Nothing in
the corpus certifies \emph{runs} --- liveness (every orbit eventually earns a certificate), amortized
or transfinite cost over unbounded time, covers that must move with their targets, obstructions that
grow, react, or are manufactured by the system's own history, route defects that integrate into
potentials, transport that emerges from substrate dynamics, or content that persists through repeated
loss. This paper is the catalog of exactly those laws: 13 dynamical structural laws
(G1--G13), organized in 4 clusters, each stated in the six-part normal form inherited
verbatim from Foundations~IV and each carrying a temporal quantifier that no static row possesses. The
laws were mined from eccentric mathematical problems --- Collatz, Goodstein, Egyptian fractions,
reverse-and-add, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, rule 184, Ducci, aperiodic tilings,
Hadwiger--Nelson, Apollonian packings --- treated as theorem detectors: each problem's folklore
almost-proof names a promoted object, the object's lawful descended certificate fixes a boundary
expression, and the residual surviving comparison against every existing law is the law seed. All
thirteen laws are mechanized in Mathlib-free Lean~4 with per-declaration kernel-axiom audits; six
laws are full \texttt{theorem}-grade rows and one splits into an unconditional theorem and a schema,
four are \texttt{schema}-grade with named boxed hypotheses, and three are calibration-anchored
schemas discharged end-to-end by solved classical instances. The paper solves no open problem and
claims none: Collatz, Erd\H{o}s--Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the Langton's-ant highway, Gilbreath,
and the exact chromatic number of the plane all remain open, and each law's nonclaims say so
explicitly.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The corpus is rich in currencies --- constraints, ledgers, potentials, duals --- but every one of them
is checked at an instant or across one declared comparison. What it lacks are the \emph{temporal}
currencies: the solvency question (does an unbounded run eventually earn a native descent
certificate?), the escrow question (can a changing presentation be audited by strict descent in a
well-founded carrier?), and the credit question (when does a supplied potential bound the total cost of
every finite prefix?). The three laws of this cluster record those currencies. Hidden Amortized Solvency (G1) is the
liveness law and the flagship of the catalog: it splits the eventual-solvency question into an
unconditional reduction and a conditional discharge schema whose named hypotheses are exactly what
remains open for Collatz. Transfinite Escrow (G2) is the termination law for stage-indexed runs, with
Goodstein sequences discharging the full transfinite mechanism. Amortized Potential Currency (G3) is the safety law:
the classical potential-method telescoping identity, stated as a currency with an explicit legality
gate.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G1}
\begin{description}
  \item[Collatz accelerated odd map --- conjectural flagship.] The affine ledger, the $2$-adic ghost
    $-1$, the $2^{L}-1$ shadowing family, and the cycle integrality condition are verified algebraic
    facts; liveness remains open because both boxed hypotheses are unproved
    \citep{Lagarias1985,Lagarias2010,Tao2019Collatz}.
  \item[Binary-counter increment --- calibration of the currency mechanism.] With $\Phi$ the number of
    $1$-bits, an increment across $r$ trailing ones costs $r + 1$, changes potential by $1 - r$, and
    is exactly solvent at every step; this calibrates the solvency currency, not the ghost mechanism
    \citep{Tarjan1985,CormenEtAl}.
  \item[Size-change and ranking-function termination --- calibration.] Termination analysis discharges
    local non-descent by a hidden well-founded ranking certificate --- ``promoted ledger gives native
    liveness'' as solved technology, without a Collatz-style ghost \citep{LeeJonesBenAmram2001}.
  \item[Aliquot dynamics --- conjectural folded instance.] For $s(n) = \sigma(n) - n$ the
    Catalan--Dickson question is open, and the natural currency is the whole factorization/divisor
    ledger rather than a scalar valuation --- G1 ledgers need not be one-dimensional
    \citep{GuySelfridge1975,GuyUnsolved}.
  \item[Switched and probabilistic termination certificates --- structural.] Average-dwell-time and
    ranking-supermartingale methods separate hidden average certificates from pointwise native
    progress; they become G1 instances only with an exact boundary certificate and pointwise residual
    \citep{Liberzon2003,AgrawalChatterjeeNovotny2017}.
\end{description}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The calibration is the solved base-2 instance: the orbit of $22 = 10110_2$ never reaches a binary
palindrome. Directly, $10110 \to 100011 \to 1010100 \to 1101001 \to 10110100$, and from there the
orbit enters a four-phase regular family, defined for $r \ge 2$ by
\[
  P_0(r) = 10\,1^r\,01\,0^r, \quad
  P_1(r) = 11\,0^{r-2}\,1\,000\,1^{r-2}\,01, \quad
  P_2(r) = 10\,1^r\,01\,0^{r+1}, \quad
  P_3(r) = 11\,0^r\,10\,1^{r-1}\,01,
\]
with the phase cycle, verified by binary addition with carries,
\[
  R(P_0(r)) = P_1(r), \qquad
  R(P_1(r)) = P_2(r), \qquad
  R(P_2(r)) = P_3(r), \qquad
  R(P_3(r)) = P_0(r+1).
\]
No string in the family is a palindrome: $P_0$ and $P_2$ begin with $1$ and end with $0$; $P_1$ and
$P_3$ begin with $11$ and end with $01$, so second and penultimate digits differ. The four pre-entry
strings are also non-palindromic, so the whole orbit is certified target-free --- discharging
\textup{[H-G5-closed-pattern]} with the full four-phase family as the invariant (note the closure is
cyclic phase-to-phase; the frequently quoted pattern $10\,1^k\,01\,0^k$ recurs under $R^4$, every
fourth iterate, not under single steps).\footnote{The base-2 result is recorded at OEIS A060382 and
attributed to Kevin Brown's MathPages note; no peer-reviewed publication of the proof was located, so
the attribution is informally sourced --- and this Kevin Brown is distinct from the Cornell
topologist Kenneth~S.~Brown, with whom secondary discussions sometimes conflate him
\citep{OEIS-A060382,Brown-MathPages}.} For base 10, no analogous certificate is known: $196$ remains
open, and finite searches, however deep, are bounded evidence only \citep{Walker-Fourmilab}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G9}
\begin{description}
  \item[Rule 184 and traffic cellular automata --- calibration.] The solved density regimes above are
    the calibration instance discharging the census-to-transport mechanism
    \citep{Fuks1997,Nagel1996,ChowdhurySantenSchadschneider2000}.
  \item[Langton's ant --- conjectural.] The highway conjecture --- that every finite initial
    configuration reaches the $104$-step highway --- remains open; the standard ant is due to
    \citet{Langton1986}. What \emph{is} proved is trajectory unboundedness, due to
    \citet{BunimovichTroubetzkoy1992}; the rival ``Cohen--Kong theorem'' attribution circulating in
    popular accounts is flagged as incorrect by the specialist literature and is not used here. The
    unboundedness fragment is a nonclaim-scoped citation: G9's theorem and lab are carried by rule
    184, not by the ant.
  \item[Excitable-media automata --- structural.] Greenberg--Hastings-style systems produce discrete
    waves and spiral cores, but an instance requires an explicit defect census and transporter
    recurrence record for a specific model \citep{Greenberg1978,DurrettGriffeath}.
  \item[Cellular-automata glider ecology --- structural.] Life gliders and one-dimensional CA
    particles are direct recurrence-with-displacement objects once the period/displacement equality is
    checked on finite support; arbitrary debris-to-glider emergence remains model-specific
    \citep{Gardner1970,Pivato}.
  \item[Queue clearing and traffic shock waves --- structural.] Kinematic-wave and cell-transmission
    models supply moving jam and clearing-front analogues; an instance requires a discrete event
    ledger matching creation, annihilation, and absorption of queue defects
    \citep{LighthillWhitham1955,Richards1956,Daganzo1994}.
\end{description}

source_wording_tex:
\subsection*{Layer instantiations}\label{layer-inst:G9}
\begin{description}
  \item[Rule 184 and traffic cellular automata --- calibration.] The solved density regimes above are
    the calibration instance discharging the census-to-transport mechanism
    \citep{Fuks1997,Nagel1996,ChowdhurySantenSchadschneider2000}.
  \item[Langton's ant --- conjectural.] The highway conjecture --- that every finite initial
    configuration reaches the $104$-step highway --- remains open; the standard ant is due to
    \citet{Langton1986}. What \emph{is} proved is trajectory unboundedness, due to
    \citet{BunimovichTroubetzkoy1992}; the rival ``Cohen--Kong theorem'' attribution circulating in
    popular accounts is flagged as incorrect by the specialist literature and is not used here. The
    unboundedness fragment is a nonclaim-scoped citation: G9's theorem and lab are carried by rule
    184, not by the ant.
  \item[Excitable-media automata --- structural.] Greenberg--Hastings-style systems produce discrete
    waves and spiral cores, but an instance requires an explicit defect census and transporter
    recurrence record for a specific model \citep{Greenberg1978,DurrettGriffeath}.
  \item[Cellular-automata glider ecology --- structural.] Life gliders and one-dimensional CA
    particles are direct recurrence-with-displacement objects once the period/displacement equality is
    checked on finite support; arbitrary debris-to-glider emergence remains model-specific
    \citep{Gardner1970,Pivato}.
  \item[Queue clearing and traffic shock waves --- structural.] Kinematic-wave and cell-transmission
    models supply moving jam and clearing-front analogues; an instance requires a discrete event
    ledger matching creation, annihilation, and absorption of queue defects
    \citep{LighthillWhitham1955,Richards1956,Daganzo1994}.
\end{description}

conclusion: This paper solves no open problem and reports no progress on one. Specifically: the Collatz conjecture remains open (G1's Part (b) hypotheses [H-G1-ghost-convergence] and [H-G1-separation] are named obligations, and the 2^L - 1 shadowing family is evidence against fixed-depth strategies, not evidence about the conjecture); Tao's almost-all result retains status probabilistic relative to G1's pointwise target and discharges neither hypothesis. The ErdH o s–Straus conjecture remains open (Mordell-style residue coverage and the quadratic-residue obstruction are sub-results about identity families; density evidence is never upgraded to pointwise closure). No base-10 Lychrel candidate is decided — 196 remains open, and deep finite searches stay bounded evidence. Recam\'an coverage remains open ( 852655 is a bounded-census fact, not a permanent-hole proof). The Langton's-ant highway conjecture remains open (trajectory unboundedness is proved, by Bunimovich–Troubetzkoy, and is cited in a nonclaim-scoped role only). Gilbreath's conjecture remains open (the gap-smallness reframing is heuristic). The exact chromatic number of the plane remains open (the bracket is 5 – 7 ). The Catalan–Dickson question for aliquot sequences remains open. Where a law names a conjectural flagship, the law organizes the problem's structure; it never claims progress on the problem itself.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Many mathematical frameworks come with audit data alongside their
main objects: source ledgers, route registries, residual budgets,
status annotations, nonclaim boundaries, and meta-audit records.
\emph{Audited Operational Realisability} (AOR) is the meta-theory of
typed carriers that close as audit systems within a declared scope.
A \emph{PreSB carrier} is a typed carrier together with this audit
data; it is an \emph{AOR carrier} when every declared audit
obligation is discharged inside the scope.  We show that every PreSB
carrier \(\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}\) admits a canonical completion into
the full subcategory of AOR carriers via a reflection
\(\mathrm{Cl}_{SB}\dashv\iota\) obtained as a monotone Knaster--Tarski
saturation on the complete lattice of AOR-extending operations.  The
reflection is developed in four parts: the closure-completion
construction and its universal property; the eight-stratum
decomposition of the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\); the thirteen-type
residual atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, its
discharge cascades, and cascade-stable AOR; and refinement chains with asymptotic
statuses, yielding the hierarchy
\(\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{casc}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}\).  The
development is meta-theoretic and carries no PDE-specific worked
example; concrete AOR-instance applications belong to consumer
manuscripts that cite this meta-theory at paper level.  Two scope
disclosures apply.  The cascade-confluence theorem uses Newman's lemma
as a classical body input after proving the local diamond property and
the well-founded discharge relation; Appendix~D records the corresponding
formal companion row as partial.  The hierarchy is exhibited via named
witness carriers and their typed obstruction markers; full predicate-level
non-membership proofs at every level remain framework future work.

conclusion: A foundation that grows by lawful extension must have undecided questions: they are the predicates not yet definable from the current lens, the places where extension is still available. The continuum hypothesis is the canonical such place (S ): the same substrate admits an inner-model packaging where it holds and a generic-extension packaging where it fails, and the ground lens does not adjudicate. Independence is the footprint of the extension law—the formal signature of a foundation that is still, lawfully, being written. A foundation with no independent questions would be one that had saturated completely, and by the saturation law no sufficiently expressive one ever does.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
There are \(|Y|^{|Y|}=3^3=27\) candidates in \(\operatorname{End}(Y)\).  Suppose one of
them satisfies \(H^2=F\).  Since \(F\) is bijective, \(H^2\) is bijective; on
a finite set this forces \(H\) itself to be bijective.  Thus the original
27-case check reduces to the six permutations of \(Y\).  Now \(F\) is the
transposition exchanging \(1\) and \(-1\) while fixing \(0\), so \(F\) is odd.
But the square of any permutation is even, because
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(H^2)=\operatorname{sgn}(H)^2=1.
\]
Hence no permutation \(H\) can satisfy \(H^2=F\), and therefore no endomorphism
of \(Y\) can do so.  A full enumeration of the original 27 candidates is
deferred to \Cref{app:methods}; the same finite check is verified in Lean as
a faithful computational proof (\Cref{app:formalization}).
\end{proof}

\(q:X\twoheadrightarrow Y\) has \(|X|\geq 3\).  If \(|X|=3\) then \(q\) is
bijective, in which case every update \(G:X\to X\) descends via
\(G^\sharp:=qGq^{-1}\), contradicting \(G\not\downarrow_q\).  Hence
\(|X|\geq 4\).  The four-phase carrier realizes this lower bound:
\Cref{lem:imag-G-nondescends} gives \(G\not\downarrow_q\) and
\Cref{lem:imag-G2-descends} gives \(G^2\downarrow_q F\).  The full
small-cardinality enumeration is deferred to \Cref{app:methods}.
\end{proof}

Within finite typed audited promoted-use traces, the paper supplies a
profile-level account of strict mathematical usefulness.  What this opens for
further work is a disciplined way to ask whether a family of lower problems
is covered by recurring audited profiles.

\begin{definition}[Explanatory compression]
\label{def:sau-explanatory-compression}
Suppose a finite registry \(\mathcal R\) SAU-covers a finite problem family \(\mathcal P\).  The registry provides \emph{explanatory compression} when many problem instances are certified by fewer recurring profile skeletons.  A crude count is
\[
\chi_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal R)=|\mathcal P|-|\mathcal R|,
\]
with the understanding that this number is only a bookkeeping index, not an invariant of mathematical depth.
\end{definition}

conclusion: The results give a theorem-grade normal form for strict mathematical usefulness in finite typed audited promoted-use traces: when a saturated lower problem is solved or certified by essentially using promoted-only structure, the trace forces hidden non-descent: a support that does not descend directly, together with an audited boundary expression that does descend. The four canonical witnesses—imaginary numbers, dual numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology—instantiate distinct minimal or universal profiles, and the necessity–soundness chain extracts SAU from strict useful traces rather than stipulating it. The no-overreading discipline blocks the literalization of hidden promoted objects in the lower layer. The scope is bounded. We address strict useful promoted-use traces, not mathematics in general; not every promoted extension is useful, and the four canonical witnesses are not an exhaustive classification of useful structures. We do not claim novelty for the classical constructions themselves, and hidden promoted objects are not asserted as lower-layer content. The companion Lean development plays a bounded role: it supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and definitional fragments and records the remaining theorems as proof-carrying traceability records. Source, Lean code, and reproducibility artifacts are hosted at ; see for the discipline that governs which results carry substantive Lean proofs. Foundations I–III provide inherited provenance but are not prerequisites for reading the paper.

source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
The forward direction is immediate from validation: a validated package has
passed each of the six witness checks, so each failure component is empty.  For
the converse, the six verified witness fields supply saturation, strictness,
non-descent, descent, solving, and audit safety, while
\(\mathbf F_{\SAU}(\mathfrak C)=\varnothing\) records that none of the
corresponding failure conditions remains open.  Hence the package validates.
This theorem is tracked by the formalization harness as a projection over the
validated-package predicate and the six failure fields.
\end{proof}

conclusion: A full enumeration of the original 27 candidates is deferred to .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
There are \(|Y|^{|Y|}=3^3=27\) candidates in \(\operatorname{End}(Y)\).  Suppose one of
them satisfies \(H^2=F\).  Since \(F\) is bijective, \(H^2\) is bijective; on
a finite set this forces \(H\) itself to be bijective.  Thus the original
27-case check reduces to the six permutations of \(Y\).  Now \(F\) is the
transposition exchanging \(1\) and \(-1\) while fixing \(0\), so \(F\) is odd.
But the square of any permutation is even, because
\[
\operatorname{sgn}(H^2)=\operatorname{sgn}(H)^2=1.
\]
Hence no permutation \(H\) can satisfy \(H^2=F\), and therefore no endomorphism
of \(Y\) can do so.  A full enumeration of the original 27 candidates is
deferred to \Cref{app:methods}.  The same finite check is verified in Lean as
a faithful computational proof; see also \Cref{app:formalization} for the Lean
traceability.
\end{proof}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{proof}
In the declared real-shadow problem, \(Y=\{-1,0,1\}\), so any surjection
\(q:X\twoheadrightarrow Y\) has \(|X|\geq 3\).  If \(|X|=3\), then \(q\) is
bijective.  In that case every update \(G:X\to X\) descends, by defining
\[
G^\sharp=qGq^{-1}:Y\to Y
\]
and observing that \(qG=G^\sharp q\).  This contradicts \(G\not\downarrow_q\).
Thus any such non-descending strict phase promotion has \(|X|\geq 4\).  The
four-phase carrier \(C_4\) has four elements, \Cref{lem:imag-G-nondescends}
gives \(G\not\downarrow_q\), and \Cref{lem:imag-G2-descends} gives
\(G^2\downarrow_q F\).  The full small-cardinality enumeration is deferred to
\Cref{app:methods}.  Lean verifies the no-same-layer-root component, here
corresponding to the lower bound on \(|X|\); the universal \(|X|\geq 4\)
statement is delivered as a paper-side argument.
\end{proof}

Within the scope of finite typed audited promoted-use traces, the paper gives a
profile-level explanation of strict mathematical usefulness.  What this unlocks
for further work is not a catalog of future domains, but a disciplined way to ask
whether a family of lower problems is covered by recurring audited profiles.

\begin{definition}[Explanatory compression]
\label{def:sau-explanatory-compression}
Suppose a finite registry \(\mathcal R\) SAU-covers a finite problem family \(\mathcal P\).  The registry provides \emph{explanatory compression} when many problem instances are certified by fewer recurring profile skeletons.  A crude count is
\[
\chi_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal R)=|\mathcal P|-|\mathcal R|,
\]
with the understanding that this number is only a bookkeeping index, not an invariant of mathematical depth.
\end{definition}

conclusion: The contribution is a theorem-grade normal form for strict mathematical usefulness in finite typed audited promoted-use traces. When a saturated lower problem is solved or certified by essentially using promoted-only structure, the trace forces hidden support that does not descend directly and an audited boundary expression that does descend. The four canonical witnesses–imaginary numbers, dual numbers, Galois roots, and graph cohomology–instantiate distinct minimal or universal profiles, and the necessity-soundness chain extracts SAU from strict useful traces rather than stipulating it. The no-overreading discipline is part of the contribution: it blocks the literalization of hidden promoted objects in the lower layer. The paper does not claim that all mathematics is useful, that every promoted extension is useful, or that every useful structure has been classified. It does not claim novelty for the classical constructions themselves, and it does not claim that hidden promoted objects literally belong to the lower layer. Foundations I–III supply inherited provenance but are not prerequisites for reading the paper, because the working vocabulary is defined locally. The Lean development also has a bounded role: it supplies substantive proofs for selected direct, computational, and definitional fragments, while projection-over-record theorems are tracked as proof-carrying traceability records.

conclusion: Read philosophically: why is there something rather than nothing is, in this grammar, a well-typed open problem.
expanded_source_wording_tex: \textbf{4. Can nothing close?} Foundations~IV explicitly defers ``stability of nothing'' for want of a recognition source. Read philosophically: \emph{why is there something rather than nothing} is, in this grammar, a well-typed open problem. Does the null package survive audit? If nothing fails to close (no carrier, no records, no persistence conditions: nothing cannot \emph{keep} being nothing), then something is what that failure looks like. We flag this as the purest Tier-O speculation in the paper. But no other tradition has given the oldest question a form, as opposed to an answer or a shrug.

expanded_source_wording_tex: What happens to a civilization after the crossing is an open question, the ninth of this book, and we will not pretend to close it. But the grammar constrains the answer's shape. Wielded creation accelerates enablement-time: more strict extensions per generation, more ghosts above and more below. And the corpus's bounded-reflexivity law holds that audit capacity does not scale for free \citep{cognition}. So the era of meta-emergence poses one structural alternative, the same alternative \S\ref{sec:singularities} posed for machine minds, now at the scale of the species: \textbf{either coherence grows with creative power, or the civilization's own creations outrun its audits} and it becomes substrate to ghosts it can no longer read. A civilization past the threshold must evolve toward higher and tighter closure: wider common quotients, faster certificate flow, denser repair transport. Not as moral aspiration. As a viability condition, of the same standing as any other gate.

conclusion: The accepted strict-test families are partitions of the closed three-slot domain at each carrier. Building a proto-effect fragment would require identifying effect-shaped structure in those families that survives the foundations claim discipline; building an effect algebra would require composition-respecting operations on such effects across the three carriers; a Born valuation would require a state-functional pairing whose values respect the effect-algebra structure; and composition readiness would require the algebraic and state-side constructions to combine coherently. Each step is a separate structural construction beyond the strict-test acceptance reported in Paper 9. Under , absence of those constructions is a nonclaim boundary, not an implied consequence of the accepted tests. The blockers are constructive rather than refutative. These higher structures remain possible targets for later work; the present paper neither constructs them nor rules them out. The claim-boundary discipline of keeps them explicit as nonclaims, and the claim-boundary control of verifies on the audit side that the accepted families respect that boundary.

conclusion: The downstream structures named at the proto-effect outcome lattice rung are future-work targets in Paper 10, not negative results or hidden refutations. A proto-effect fragment would require accepted packages on which candidate operations can be probed. An effect algebra would require a proto-effect-level operation structure with enough closure and compatibility to support algebraic organization. A Born valuation would require an admissible valuation target over that event/proto-effect structure. Composition readiness would require enough accepted package and operation data to support lawful composition. None of these inputs is supplied by Paper 10, because the event-package candidate stage is upstream-blocked before any such downstream test can begin. The absence of proto-effect, effect-algebra, Born, and composition results is a structural input absence. Proto-effect probes inherit no support because no package is promoted and no accepted package is available as input ( ). These targets sit after accepted event-level records, package candidates, and promotion in the dependency order.

source_wording_digest: What remains open is therefore clear. First, the lens robustness of the P4-active classes should be improved beyond the canonical manual channel. Second, the asymptotic status of the classes—whether they correspond to distinct stabilized universality classes, or to a smaller number of exponent-level classes decorated by secondary fields—remains unresolved. Third, broader upstream coverage is needed if the taxonomy is to be claimed as more than a controlled synthetic-and-bridged program. These are real open problems, but they are now posed against a cleaner background than before. The paper leaves the field with a controlled rubric, a confirmed set of low-complexity classes, and an observable map that future work will have to respect. Conclusion

The freeze is intentionally selective. It does not attempt to preserve every intermediate artifact, every raw exploratory output, or every optional development branch in the repository. Nor does it treat optional future work as pending evidence. In particular, no further Lean expansion, no further broad experimental sweeps, and no additional post-freeze evidence-collection steps are presumed by the manuscript. The writing phase therefore starts from a bounded scientific object: the experiment is frozen, the claim surface is frozen, and the manuscript is not waiting on further implementation.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{description}
\item[T17-S (simplified certificate schema).] \textsf{[S]} structural schema.
Lean defines a carrier-indexed \emph{simplified} certificate
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X)$: mechanics-based clause predicates C1--C8 over one declared
transition/action family and lens family (the C1/C5/C6/C8 audit objects are
equation-coupled to the declared mechanics; C4/C7 are structurally
constrained on the same support but not transition-coupled, a schema-grade
distinction recorded explicitly), cross-clause coherence requiring one
nonempty communicating viable hub containing the clause witnesses, and a
simplified promotion ledger. The schemas are not ordered by any landed
theorem: $\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}$ uses a weaker imported gate ledger while adding one-step
restrictions absent from the full design definition; no implication or
equivalence between $\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}$ and $\mathfrak{C}$ has been proved or is claimed,
and no integrated instance is exhibited. T17-S does not claim its schema
suffices for lawful closure or consciousness; that is exactly the
additional purchase in T17-O.
\item[T17-P (witness catalog and hygiene protocol).] \textsf{[S]}
protocol/catalog. The Python protocol imports and re-verifies eight per-law
witness fields (one row per clause, sourced from the landed laws of
Sections~\ref{sec:t1}--\ref{sec:clusters}) and recursively scans stored
condition-bearing values for smuggled vocabulary. Every current row carries
the verdict \texttt{witness\_verified}; no row label is a realization
verdict, and the protocol constructs no candidate, no integrated carrier, no
gate-panel object, and no realization result.
\item[T17-M (simplified certificate contrast).] \textsf{[S]} schema. Lean
defines $\mathrm{SimplifiedCertificateContrast}(a,b) :=
\mathrm{PublicMatch}(a,b) \wedge \mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(a) \wedge \neg\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(b)$:
dynamic public-statistics matching over the complete public observation, a
simplified certificate for $a$, and its absence for $b$. This is an
explicitly simplified approximation of T4b's demarcation target, not the
full-certificate relation, which remains open until a full certificate
exists.
\item[T17-O (conditional realization bridge).] \textsf{[O]} axiom-relative
conditional schema; the exact logical form is displayed below.
\item[T17-I (integrated instance).] \textsf{[OPEN]}. The required deliverable is
absent: an exhibited carrier and package satisfying a \emph{full} design-level
certificate, together with a \emph{proved} (not assumed) certificate-soundness
theorem. Both artifacts record this explicitly: Lean pins
$\texttt{singleCarrierInstanceExhibited}=\texttt{false}$ and Python pins the
same flag with realization grade \texttt{schema}.
\item[T17a (report-interface pointer).] \textsf{[S]} interface-relative pointer.
On the finite T3/T9 carrier, hidden no-report content does not factor through
the declared report channel. This says nothing about whether a designer could
specify or predict content from the complete state, initial conditions, or
dynamics.
\item[T17b (declared-interface opacity pointer).] \textsf{[S]}
interface-relative pointer. Relative to the declared current channels, T2's
hidden structure does not descend and T9 blocks overreading the report
boundary. Opacity may disappear under an expanded interface (T2's own
dissolution control demonstrates this); this is not opacity to every creator
or instrument, and it carries no moral-status conclusion.
\end{description}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\subsection{Outlook}
Three directions follow naturally. First, extend the substrate to multi-agent settings where P$_2$ constraints and P$_4$ tokens can encode commitments, ownership, and norms. Second, move from exact kernels to approximate learned models while preserving the audit posture (hashing, manifests, and invariants). Third, explore alternative causal proxies (risk-sensitive empowerment, reachability volumes, intervention-based causal effect sizes) and characterize when they agree or disagree.

expanded_source_wording_tex: The contribution is a code-backed feasibility study asking whether compositional structure in a fixed Shakespeare corpus can be recovered as a finite ladder of certified theory refinements. In bounded runs, the runtime builds typed audited layers, records promotion attempts and failures, emits halt verdicts, caps unaudited fallback readout, and demonstrates strict layer growth without turning every signal into a claim; \Cref{sec:primary-results} reports those runtime results. Independent of the runtime, a structural probe suite tests framework-level commitments under blue-team and red-team cases covering growth, forgetting, uncertainty, auditability, and concept separation; \Cref{sec:secondary-results} separates those probes from the Shakespeare run. The scope is deliberately narrower than a full dynamical theory of interacting layers. This paper studies constructive bottom-up native growth on a static-parent substrate: it operates in a frozen-parent regime, with live parent dynamics deferred to future work, and with bidirectional inter-layer substrate flow not modelled. \Cref{sec:discussion} states these as limitations rather than treating them as implementation details.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Dependency relations and active relation kinds.}\label{subsec:dep-relations}
The audit ledger also records a typed dependency relation for each committed child layer. We use the dependency-relation vocabulary from the SBT admissibility calculus, whose full form declares eight relation kinds \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII}. In this paper, only upward layer-birth dependence is active: the parent's audit surface enables the child's strict extension. This restricted relation is sufficient for the static-parent setting because every committed native layer is justified as a child extension of the previous audited surface, not as a claim about parent revision or bidirectional flow. Other relation kinds are deferred to future work and appear as paper-level limitations in \Cref{sec:discussion}; \Cref{app:formalization} lists the full vocabulary.

This calls for an explicit anti-relabeling stance.  This paper does not claim
the folk theorems, global games, reputation models, stochastic stability,
correlated equilibrium, Bayesian types, Markov states, or causal-state
quotients as its own results.  Those literatures are reference points: each
shows a way in which additional structure can matter.  The contribution here is the
certified inter-layer account that connects them without collapsing them into
one another: a canonical predictive institution, exact information-theoretic
price, finite non-definability certificates, material-feedback tests, and a
registered run/data program.  The strict-extension, predictive-quotient, and
closure-deficit theorem layers are imported from the cited source papers and
instantiated here on the declared carrier
\citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This conjunction also answers the three questions posed at the start, within
the declared scope.  What is an institution?  In this paper it is the canonical
predictive state of repeated play: the coarsest history summary sufficient for
the declared future.  When does the bare game predict behavior?  Exactly when
the stage vocabulary is closed, equivalently when its closure deficit is zero;
when the deficit is positive, the missing predictive information has an exact
price.  Where does the structure come from?  On the finite carrier, it appears
where the stage layer discards predictive information, can be made active only
under live non-stage-definable feedback, and produces run constants that are
reachable by running the process rather than by the tested low-complexity
shortcuts.  In the analyzed data, the corresponding residue is present, while
its timing points away from the fixed-population formation picture and toward
acquisition with experience.  These statements are scoped to the declared
carrier, declared run families and protocols, and the analyzed dataset; the
broader framework theorems are imported and cited, not re-proved here.

conclusion: Outlook.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\paragraph{Outlook.}
The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition
carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the
sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency \citep{Tsiokos2026ThrowStone}.  The
failed crystallization bridge in
\Cref{subsec:crystallization-bridge} shows that experience-as-composition
selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable,
whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience.  A carrier
in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories
would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open.  A second direction
is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory
beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become
genuinely coherent.  A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate:
richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public
signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the
minimal catalog.

conclusion: The most direct next construction is a within-agent learning or acquisition carrier, in which the individual agent is treated as a carrier object in the sense of the Six Birds treatment of agency . The failed crystallization bridge in shows that experience-as-composition selection makes the finite carrier more homogeneous and more stage-predictable, whereas the data show history-dependence growing with experience. A carrier in which individual agents acquire conditional rules over their own histories would test the mechanism that this contrast leaves open. A second direction is a broader family of noisy and dissipative carriers, to map route memory beyond the tested noise grid and to learn when currentizable traces become genuinely coherent. A third is to enlarge the strategic and payoff substrate: richer automata, larger action spaces, asymmetric games, and longer public signals would test which carrier facts persist and which are artifacts of the minimal catalog. The run layer also invites a bounded-rationality connection. The imitation dynamics used here contain a logit-style temperature parameter; in a maximum-entropy or shadow-price reading, such a parameter can be interpreted as the dual of a binding cognitive or informational budget rather than a free behavioral knob . That connection is only an opening in this paper, but it suggests how run-only constants might be tied to explicit resource constraints. On the empirical side, the immediate extension is broader pre-registered testing of the residue hypothesis and the timing reversal on other repeated-game datasets, with the same discipline: hypotheses, predictors, bands, folds, and amendments fixed before outcome analysis.

conclusion: The scope is deliberately limited: BSD and Hodge are out of scope except as future work or prediction, and no substrate closure is strengthened here to a standard-ZFC unconditional claim.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Six Birds Theory has produced three landed Clay-class conditional
closures: Navier--Stokes regularity, the Riemann Hypothesis, and
P~vs~NP, each under the SB closure assumption of Foundations~I.  This
paper does not re-prove those substrate results.  It extracts their
common meta-theoretic form for a reader who treats Six Birds as a
typed framework for organizing attempted closures of open conjectures.
The account has two complementary halves.  The negative half,
Foreclosure, studies a typed primary carrier, meaning an attempted
proof construction whose type signature targets a designated
conjecture, and proves that admissible carriers fall into a finite
state space: non-target-equivalent, target-equivalent tautological,
bridge-failed, or matrix-element-terminal.  The positive half,
Recognition-Mode Landing, gives a seven-stage route for
trace-state-only substrates: instead of deriving the load-bearing
source from framework primitives, it imports that source as named
recognition under closure formation.  The v5 refinement states the
joint thesis: derivation routes remain subject to foreclosure, while
recognition-mode landings are structurally distinct peer routes under
the same closure assumption.  A third part, the Calibration Family,
provides the typed bookkeeping that makes this comparison uniform
across substrates: calibrations, bridges-as-theorems, directed bridge
types, coverage geometry, framework-type mismatch, and named
functorial gates.  Layer-instantiation examples appear throughout: the
three substrate validation rows (NS, RH, and PvNP), a thirteen-entry
calibration seed catalog of typed detectors, two named coverage holes,
and three named functorial gates from the PvNP track.  The formal
catalog contains seventeen rows: three partial structural derivations,
eight primary theorem-grade rows, and six primary obligation rows.  The body gives the mathematical proofs or
obligation analyses, while Lean serves as the mechanization companion
and audit trail.  The nine honest obligation axioms are

A closure formation is the background act of organizing an open
problem, its admissible source material, and the claimed closure event
inside one formal setting.  In this paper the framework-native name is
\textsc{Foundations~I}\ closure formation, and we use it only as a black-box import from

closure is therefore a formal closure of an open problem in which the
closure event is itself treated as a structural fact about the
problem's mathematical setting, rather than as an informal label
attached after the fact to a proof.  The SB closure assumption is the
\textsc{Foundations~I}\ closure-formation working axiom under which all substrate
landings cited in this paper are stated.  It is not a
standard-ZFC-unconditional claim, and it is not re-proved here.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The open problem is to identify a substrate-independent invariant
that would bound CTMT depth across cascades.  Candidate invariants
could measure inherited-record complexity, descent height, native
matrix-family rank, or some future refinement of the carrier's
adequacy residual.  Any such proposal would need to be compatible with
the recursive constructor of \Cref{thm:ctmt-recursion}: a depth bound
cannot merely rule out further reductions by definition; it must
explain why the next deeper matrix-element family cannot arise under
the typed-context discipline.

conclusion: The formal inductive definition of basis generation, together with the normal-class assignment, is deferred to .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
A feature is \emph{basis-generated} when it is built from
\(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{fix}}\) by finitely many applications of the
allowed closure operations: quotienting, orbiting, transporting,
holonomy or gluing-class formation, pairing, products, polynomial
post-processing, resource filtration, and presentation refinement.  Each
basis-generated feature is assigned a normal class.  The quotient class
\(Q\) records an equivalence relation that the proposed Class-B law
requires every lawful current observable to respect.  The joint-access
class \(J\) records a tuple of separately current observables whose
joint access is alleged to be inadmissible.  The positive-closure class
\(C\) records a construction yielding new current observables from
current ones.  The presentation-refinement class \(P\) records a
refinement of the carrier by presentation data; it supplies breaker
data, not an obstruction.  The time-filtration class \(T\) records a
feature indexed by polynomial resource strata.  The Basis Combination
Closure theorem in the next subsection proves that these five classes
are exhaustive for basis-generated features.  The formal inductive
definition of basis generation, together with the normal-class
assignment, is deferred to \Cref{app:class-b-definitions}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
In practice this motivates two families of tests:
(i)~\emph{scale-cut or smoothing sweeps}, in which one varies the effective lens scale and re-runs inference/audits, and
(ii)~\emph{probe splits}, in which one fits on a subset of observables and predicts another.
We demonstrated the mechanics of these tests in both synthetic settings and in public-vector LSS audits, with an explicit limitation that the current LSS results use a surrogate backend (Limitation~\ref{box:surrogate_lss}) and should not be read as physical parameter constraints.
The staging sweep on DES Y3 vectors is therefore recorded as supplementary protocol evidence (Appendix~\ref{app:lss_scale_cut}), while physical staging interpretation is deferred to a backend-enabled analysis.
Operationally, a staging fingerprint would be a structured, reproducible dependence of the inferred correction (or of cross-probe predictive bias) on lens-scale choices (e.g., scale cuts, smoothing windows, summary-statistic definitions) that (a)~persists across reasonable reanalyses, (b)~changes directionally with probe splits, and (c)~correlates with independent heterogeneity proxies when available.
Absent these controls, staging dependence can be an observational systematic rather than a closure signature; our emphasis is therefore on probe-split audits and robustness suites rather than on any single scale-sweep curve.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Several follow-on experiments would strengthen both the physics-like narrative and the algebraic/PICA contribution.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Controlled-$\tau$ reruns.} Run matched-$\tau$ sweeps (or fixed-$\tau$ protocols) for Baseline vs Full conditions to separate closure effects from timescale effects.
  \item \textbf{Alternative lenses and lifts.} Repeat the multiscale scan with alternative coarse-graining constructions (e.g., different spectral clustering variants) and non-uniform lifts $Q_f$ (e.g., conditional stationary lifts) to test lens robustness.
  \item \textbf{Scaling.} Extend to larger $n$ and larger $k$ ladders, and test whether the regime separation sharpens, merges, or transitions.
  \item \textbf{Ablation completion.} Add ablations that remove the two currently untested spectral core cells (or replace them with alternative partition primitives) to complete the generator picture.
  \item \textbf{Audit stress tests.} Vary path horizon $T$, embedding dimension $m$, and regularization floors to quantify audit stability and reduce confounds.
  \item \textbf{Cross-substrate transfer.} Apply the disciplined PICA cell catalog to other substrates. The six primitives have been used on particle-based and neural/meta-layer toy substrates \cite{Tsiokos2026Life}, but with additional non-PICA mechanisms; re-implementing those substrates under strict PICA closure would test whether similar regimes emerge without extra assumptions and whether generator subalgebras transfer.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Directed versus undirected.}
If we use the directed cost $c_\eta(x\to y)$, then the resulting $d_\eta(x,y)$ need not equal $d_\eta(y,x)$; mathematically this is a directed shortest-path distance (a quasi-metric or directed pseudo-distance).  In this paper we default to an undirected geometry by symmetrizing before converting to costs, yielding a symmetric distance suitable for comparison with familiar geometric regimes.  Directed geometries induced by asymmetric feasibility (constraints) are natural in the SBT framework but are deferred to future work.
